genxml.title: TIOCE (TIO PCI Express bridge), as SGI's Linux Altix platform code defines it
genxml.doc: Names and offsets are the definitions of SGI's Linux Altix platform code (header and provider, v5.3). The TIOCE's own register specification is not held. The header gives no access direction and no reset value for any register; rows say what the provider does where it touches one. Bit layouts the header defines are fields of their registers. Where the header names a register with its masks (interrupt status and mask, error summary and mask, force interrupt, the upstream engine control, page map, pipe select and mask, PCIe control, gearbox configuration, downstream engine configuration) the fields are established; the same layout on a sibling register (an alias, say) is inferred and said so on the register. Constants keep the plain values (identifiers, address windows, enhanced configuration masks).

struct.name: ADM_ID
struct.doc: Widget identification word: part 0xce00, source id 1, revision A = 1 (header constants). Revision A needs the access workaround described on the unit page. Name and offset are the vendor header's definition (struct member ce_adm_id). The header gives no access direction or reset value; access rw is a placeholder.

struct.name: ADM_INT_STATUS
struct.doc: Interrupt status. Bit n is the interrupt source named by the header (error, link 1 and 2 errors, PCIe error, hot-plug events per port, INTA to INTD of each port, message slots 0 to 3, power-management events). The provider reads it on revision A before forcing an interrupt. Name and offset are the vendor header's definition (struct member ce_adm_int_status). The header gives no access direction or reset value; access rw is a placeholder. Field layout: the header defines the bit position of every source. Bit 14 is also named as the first message slot. Bits 18 to 21 and above 23 have no definition.

struct.name: ADM_INT_STATUS_ALIAS
struct.doc: Interrupt status alias. The provider sets every bit through it at attach to clear transients (the alias is the write path to clear; role from that use). Name and offset are the vendor header's definition (struct member ce_adm_int_status_alias). The header gives no access direction or reset value; access rw is a placeholder. Field layout is inferred: the header gives positions only for the status and mask registers. The provider writes all ones here at attach, after a load and OR, to clear stale interrupts, which reads as a write-to-clear alias of the status word (inferred from the provider comment, not stated by the header).

struct.name: ADM_INT_MASK
struct.doc: Interrupt mask. The provider sets a source bit, writes its destination, then clears the bit, so a set bit blocks the source while the destination is rewritten. Name and offset are the vendor header's definition (struct member ce_adm_int_mask). The header gives no access direction or reset value; access rw is a placeholder. Field layout: the header defines these positions for the mask and the status register alike. The provider sets a bit before retargeting a source and clears it afterwards.

struct.name: ADM_INT_PENDING
struct.doc: Name and offset are the vendor header's definition (struct member ce_adm_int_pending). The header gives no access direction or reset value; access rw is a placeholder.

struct.name: ADM_FORCE_INT
struct.doc: Force interrupt. Bits 0 to 7 force INTA to INTD of port 1 then port 2; bit 8 forces always. The bit numbering differs from the status register, and the provider maps explicitly. Revision A does not use it (workaround). Name and offset are the vendor header's definition (struct member ce_adm_force_int). The header gives no access direction or reset value; access rw is a placeholder. Field layout from the header: bits 0 to 7 are the four interrupt pins of each port, bit 8 forces unconditionally. These positions differ from the status register, and the provider maps between them explicitly.

struct.name: ADM_URE_UPS_BUF_BARRIER_FLUSH
struct.doc: Name and offset are the vendor header's definition (struct member ce_adm_ure_ups_buf_barrier_flush). The header gives no access direction or reset value; access rw is a placeholder. Field layout: the header gives only the shift of each of eight selectors (one per pipe of each port), spaced four bits apart. The four-bit width is inferred from the spacing. The provider never touches it.

struct.name: ADM_INT_DEST
struct.doc: Interrupt destination, one per source (the header declares fifteen). The provider writes the kernel vector in bits 63:56 (shift INTR_VECTOR_SHFT) ORed with the destination coretalk address of the target CPU, indexed by interrupt source bit. Name and offset are the vendor header's definition (struct member ce_adm_int_dest). The header gives no access direction or reset value; access rw is a placeholder. The vector field is inferred: the header gives only the shift 56 and the provider ORs the vector over the destination address; bit 63 as the top is the end of the word, not a header fact. The extent of the address part is unknown.

struct.name: ADM_ERROR_SUMMARY
struct.doc: Name and offset are the vendor header's definition (struct member ce_adm_error_summary). The header gives no access direction or reset value; access rw is a placeholder. Field layout from the header: one bit per error source, bits 0 to 61.

struct.name: ADM_ERROR_SUMMARY_ALIAS
struct.doc: Error summary alias. The provider sets every bit through it at attach to clear transient errors. Name and offset are the vendor header's definition (struct member ce_adm_error_summary_alias). The header gives no access direction or reset value; access rw is a placeholder. Field layout is inferred: the header assigns bits to the summary and mask registers only. The provider writes all ones here at attach with the same clear-transient-errors intent as the status alias; the one-bit-per-source layout is carried over from the summary by that role, not stated.

struct.name: ADM_ERROR_MASK
struct.doc: Name and offset are the vendor header's definition (struct member ce_adm_error_mask). The header gives no access direction or reset value; access rw is a placeholder. Field layout from the header: same bit assignment as the summary register. The header does not say whether a set bit enables or masks the source (unknown).

struct.name: URE_PAGE_MAP
struct.doc: Upstream request engine page size map. The provider clears the page-size field and sets it to the 256 KiB encoding (4) at attach, the largest the code uses; the 32/40-bit entries are then 256 KiB pages. Name and offset are the vendor header's definition (struct member ce_ure_page_map). The header gives no access direction or reset value; access rw is a placeholder. Field layout from the header. The pagesize field holds the encodings the header names (0 to 4); 5 to 7 are unknown. The provider uses 4.

struct.name: URE_DIR_MAP
struct.doc: Upstream request engine direct map, one per port. For 32-bit direct DMA the provider stores the target's coretalk address with the low 30 bits cleared (a 1 GiB-aligned base), reads it back to flush, and refcounts users: a second user needs the same base. Name and offset are the vendor header's definition (struct member ce_ure_dir_map). The header gives no access direction or reset value; access rw is a placeholder.

struct.name: URE_PIPE_SEL1
struct.doc: Name and offset are the vendor header's definition (struct member ce_ure_pipe_sel1). The header gives no access direction or reset value; access rw is a placeholder. Three 19-bit selectors at bits 0, 20 and 40 (header selector masks). Within a selector the header defines traffic class, bus, device and function masks at bits 18:16, 15:8, 7:3 and 2:0; they sum to 19 bits. The layout is established for the first selector, whose position the macros give; for the second and third it is inferred from the identical selector width. Meaning of each selector (a source id match for a pipe) is inferred from the register name.

struct.name: URE_PIPE_MASK1
struct.doc: Name and offset are the vendor header's definition (struct member ce_ure_pipe_mask1). The header gives no access direction or reset value; access rw is a placeholder. Three 19-bit mask fields at bits 0, 20 and 40 from the header masks. That each mask applies to the selector of the same index is inferred from naming.

struct.name: URE_PIPE_SEL2
struct.doc: Name and offset are the vendor header's definition (struct member ce_ure_pipe_sel2). The header gives no access direction or reset value; access rw is a placeholder.
